Well that makes sense really. A mother separated from her child is bound to cause problems for both.

I used to work in one of the UK's largest prisoner mother and baby units. My job was sorting records, which had to be kept for 10 years after the death of the prisoner or their child, whichever was later. Some of the stories in the records were heartbreaking. Mothers who had been prostitutes that were being treated for multiple STI's during their pregnancy, then babies treated as they were born, lots and lots of babies with withdrawal symptoms at birth- in UK prisons most heroin addicts are given methadone programmes instead of going cold turkey, and it's considered safer for the baby than for the mother to go through withdrawal whilst pregnant. Lots of mothers having children that were a product of rape or sexual abuse. One of the saddest thing was that there was a catch 22 situation- that if the mother was serving a short sentence there was a good chance of her never having to be separated from her child, however the demand for places in the mother and baby unit was so high that it's considered not feasible or cost effective to move prisoners on short sentences or on remand for offences for which they may be found not guilty. I only worked there for a short time but it really opened my eyes to how awful the world is for some people.
So you mean mothers on short sentences were at greater risk of losing their children to the care system because of logistics?

Sometimes. Was very much the luck of the draw. If you only had a sentence of a couple of months in many cases they didn't feel it was worthwhile transporting you to a mother and baby unit potentially hundreds of miles away, that's if there was a place available.

Eat whatever is on this vague island, being sure to cook everything before hand in hops of removing any toxins/bacteria. Boil found water in a rock bowl, or make a primitive desalination set up using leaves to drink sea water if there is no fresh water.

First you need shelter. You will die from exposure faster than anything else. Make a small shelter out of Palm leaves and loose wood. Build this on the edge of the beach and wooded area so you only have to guard one side from wild animals. Then, build a fire on the side of your shelter that faces the jungle. This will prevent smoke from blowing into your new house, scare off animals, and keep you warm. Fire is the most important thing!! You only have so much gas in your lighter. As soon as you start a fire with small sticks and get it reasonable large, start making a dry storage for wood near your shelter. It's an island so it will rain a lot - you must have dry wood to fee your fire!

Next is water. Luckily you have a water bottle! At first drink coconut juice if you can get it open with sharp rocks. This is risky because if you cut yourself you're fucked. But if you get diarrhea from bacteria you might as well call yourself dead. If coconuts aren't available you can make a bowl by starting a small fire with coals and digging out the charcoal as it burns into the wood. The charcoal also has the added benefit of vitamins! You will hear rocks in your fire and use tongs to "boil" your water by sticking the hot rocks in your coconut/ bowl until you actually see it bubble up. (This really works) Use your actual water bottle to carry water while you work and to collect rain water. Make a large bucket (using the fire technique) to save your water. If you get injured having backup water will be life or death.

Last thing you need to think about is food. You need food. So you can collect water - the human body is a lot more resilient than you think. Fishing can be a complete waste of energy unless the environment is particularly predisposed to fishing. Focus on exploring and finding fruits that you know (bananas, sugarcane, coconuts, mangos, ect). Watch what the animals eat and test that. By test I mean put some on your lips. The next day chew a little then spit it out. The next day eat a bit. The next day eat some. If at any point it fucks with your body it's not worth it! You can survive if you've made it to this point.

Mentally you must keep yourself sane. That means always stay busy whether making rope, improving your shelter, or just exploring. Make a Wilson if you have to (Castaway reference). Keep your lighter dry and DO NOT throw it away if it stops working. The flint and steel are still useful even if it runs out of gas.

One last thing. Meat is a luxury of our modern world. Hunting and fishing are dangerous! Raw mean is dangerous! One infection and it could be the end - whether foodborne illness or hunting accident. Only seek meat once you have a comfortable schedule. Oh yeah, and keep making rope, it's super useful for camp craft and escape rafts.

  • Corruption in gaming journalism and competitions, and the resulting demand for disclosure and ethics reform.
  • * A game developer sleeping with a journalist who then gave her game very favorable reviews (when the gaming community thought the game was not very good). She also got a gaming fundraiser shut down just before starting her own gaming fundraiser.
    • A PR agent sleeping with the head judge of a game festival and her clients' games winning.

  • Outrage spreads to Twitter, among other online forums.

    • The two women above, as well as others related to the industry jump into the heated discussion online. A few receive death threats. All sides condemn harassment and threats.

  • Gaming journalists publish articles declaring "gamers are dead" and paint them as cis white male misogynists who hate women in their previously-male-dominated industry. The allegations of corruption are not addressed.

  • Gamers outraged at the "anti-gamer" sites who ran the articles stereotyping and shaming their own fan base.

  • * Gamers note that 10+ sites all ran similar talking-points on the same day, and suspect an industry-wide issue. They dig deeper into the web of industry relationships and uncover more conflicts of interest, but also a suspicion that radical, anti-male feminists (often referred to pejoratively as "social justice warriors" or SJWs) are driving the narrative in the press.
    • Gamers are upset that SJWs are deflecting the issue of corruption and turning it into one of misogyny and harassment of females in the industry. Articles that emerge in the BBC and Guardian do not mention the original issue of corruption, but focus on the death threats.

  • The female author of the Guardian article is shown to be financially supportive of the women she defends in her article. She is called out on it publicly.

  • * Gamers are convinced this is proof of the corruption.
    • SJWs are convinced this is proof of the misogyny.

  • In response to SJWs accusing the #GamerGate movement as being driven by mostly cis white males, minority gamers who support the movement tweet with #NotYourShield to tell the SJWs they don't need anyone speaking for them.

There is a lot more to be said, but this should serve as a primer.

Also note there is a 3rd party - trolls - who will fan the flames just because they can.
